title: DW3 port menus/<screen>/menu.json (menus-menu-v1)
description: The pieces of one menu screen: a PNG per rectangle of the screen's art with its palette, and where the game draws each (data/menus/<screen>/, menu.json and <piece>.png). Written by pc/shim/menu_export.c (docJson, pieceJson) and read back by pc/shim/menu_pack.c when a mod has menus/<screen>/<piece>.png: the positions come from the disc's own sheet, not from this file, so editing menu.json changes nothing; edit the PNGs (same size, at most 16 colours, 256 for mode 8bit). Detail: docs/formats.md 7.5b.

name.description: The screen: the *TM file's name without the suffix, lowercase (stmcrd, stdglb).

disc.description: Where the art comes from (no bytes).

files.description: The disc files, without the AAA/ prefix: the screen's pages (*TM.BIN) and its sheet (*CS.BIN).

unexported.description: Only when the whole document could not be cut (for example, the stage sets no sprite sheet); pieces is then empty.

pages.description: The size of each page of the screen in halfwords [width, height] (the game loads them side by side, 64 halfwords per page); null for a page that could not be read.

file.description: The piece's PNG in the same folder, f<frame>p<slot>.png (the first frame and slot that use it). null when the piece cannot be cut (see unexported); such a piece is listed so no part of the sheet is dropped silently.

unexported.description: Only with file null: why. Values the exporter writes: empty rectangle, palette outside the pages, no pixels on the pages.

page.description: The page where the piece's top-left corner falls (u / 256 in 4bit, u / 128 in 8bit).

u.description: Texels, in the space of the screen's pages laid side by side.

clut.description: The piece's palette: column x in halfwords of the screen's space, row (the frame's CLUT row included) and the page where the palette falls.

outside.description: Only written when true: the rectangle reaches past the pages (those texels are index 0). No piece of the EU disc does.

frames.description: Where the game draws the piece.

frame.description: The frame's id in the sheet.

slot.description: The part's position in the frame (slot 0 is drawn last, on top).

at.description: x, y from the sprite's origin.

blend.description: none is opaque; the others are the PS1 semi-transparency rates 0 to 3 (unknown for any other value).

notes.description: Fixed explanation, written in every export.
